PCA Rank Approximation Function

Below is the rank approximation function I created for the provided images.

library(readr)
img1 <- read_csv("image1.csv")
## Rows: 1000 Columns: 100
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## dbl (100): X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6, X7, X8, X9, X10, X11, X12, X13, X14, X15,...
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
img1 <- data.matrix(img1)
rank_k_pca_approx <- function(img, k) {
  
  n <- nrow(img)
  p <- ncol(img)
  k <- min(k, n, p) 
  
  pca <- prcomp(img, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
  
  scores_k   <- pca$x[, 1:k, drop = FALSE]        
  loadings_k <- pca$rotation[, 1:k, drop = FALSE]   
  
  approx <- scores_k %*% t(loadings_k)            
  approx <- sweep(approx, 2, pca$center, "+")        
  
  error <- norm(img - approx, type = "F")
  
  list(approximation = approx, error = error)
}

##result <- rank_k_pca_approx(img1, k = 10)
##plot(result$approximation)

Below is the plot of the first eigenvector, followed by a plot of the first PC score

Interpretation of PC1 scores and Eigenvector plots

For the PC1 score plot, each number represents how far a feature projects in the new direction. In terms of the Eigenvectors plot, each index is how much a particular variable contributes to the principal component itself.
